WHAT IT DOES

From sample to pattern.

01 / CHOP

Find the part you want.

Automatic transient chops with editable boundaries, waveform zoom, pitch, envelopes, hold loops, and latch. Two independent chop layouts share the same audio.

02 / SEQUENCE

Build it on the keys.

A paged step grid with 1–64 steps per track, four patterns, and arrangement sections. Add swing, probability, repeats, pitch locks, and conditional hits.

03 / PERFORM

Play the beat.

Choke groups, held drum rolls, and loop tempo sync. Filter, delay, chorus, reverb, and distortion, with separate compression controls.

GET STARTED

Install. Load. Play.

You need an FM1, a USB data cable, and desktop Chrome or Edge for USB MIDI. The sample editor runs locally in your browser.

  1. Back up your instrument.

    If you already run Pigeon, open the sample tool, connect the FM1, and save a complete recovery archive. Keep a copy on your computer before changing firmware.

    Open backup and sample tool ↗

  2. Install Pigeon over USB.

    Download the package below. Existing Pigeon users can select it in the sample tool’s firmware panel; the tool saves a recovery archive before writing. For stock firmware or another compatible FM1 firmware, use the dedicated installer. Keep USB connected and the instrument powered until it restarts.

    Open USB installer ↗Download firmware ↓

    Beta candidate; hardware verification is pending. An interrupted update may require recovery hardware. Review the installer’s recovery information before continuing.

  3. Bring your samples.

    Open the sample tool, import Song 1 and Song 2, and add up to 16 one-shots. Trim, preview, adjust chops, then send the combined bank to the FM1. Uploading replaces both songs and the kit together.

    Open sample editor ↗

  4. Disconnect and play.

    Use the FM1’s keys to trigger chops, edit boundaries with the knobs, and build a pattern in the sequencer. Your samples remain in flash. Keep an exported bank and project archive for recovery.

    Read the quick controls ↓

White and black keysTrigger chops; extra chops use the alternate key bank

Working with drum loops?

Use Song 2 for your break. Set the number of beats in a reference loop, then turn tempo sync on. Playback speed follows project BPM, so pitch changes with tempo.

Sync range: half to double speed. Use a full-loop chop for whole-loop playback, or sequence individual slices.

Full controls and workflow ↗

On SEQ: K1 tempo, K2 tempo/sample-end timing, K3 step, K4 length (1–64). OCT selects step duration. REC arms recording; the screen shows stopped, armed, recording, or playing. Pattern changes wait for the configured next-bar or pattern-end boundary.

KNOW YOUR SPACE

One bank. You choose the split.

Both songs and all drum pads share 408 KiB. Songs use indexed mono MP3; drum one-shots use ADPCM. Longer songs leave less room for the kit.

SONG 1
SONG 2
KIT

Illustrative allocation. With no Song 2 or drums, about 130 seconds fits at 24 kbps, or about 50 seconds at 64 kbps. The tool shows the actual space used before upload.

There are eight shared playback voices. Direct recording, resampling, and compressed reverse playback are not part of this release.

BEFORE YOU START

A few practical answers.

Does the sample tool upload my audio to a server?

No. Importing, encoding, previewing, and editing run on your computer in the browser. USB MIDI sends the bank directly to your FM1. Wait for “Offline ready” in the tool before disconnecting the internet; its cached features remain available while browser storage is retained.

Can I return to the original firmware?

Use M-VAVE’s official update procedure with an unmodified official firmware package to return to stock. Back up first: the stock firmware cannot open Pigeon projects. A loader-mode recovery needs its own recovery procedure.

Official M-VAVE downloads ↗
How is Pigeon related to Felucca?

Pigeon is an independent sampler project built on Felucca. Existing project containers remain supported, but inherited synth tracks do not sound in the sampler profile. New conditional-step data requires current Pigeon firmware.

What has been tested?

This candidate passed Pigeon product checks, sanitizer checks, codec and storage validation, and target CPU-budget checks. All 92 reference audio renders are unchanged, and repeated builds produced identical hashes. This candidate has not been flashed or verified on hardware. USB bank transfers and live playback still need physical testing. Inherited Felucca synth-screen layout checks report font-related failures; the Pigeon screen check reports no fixed-label clipping.
